title: The Tally of Dishonor
issueFunction: Financial legibility as a modern form of status and participation. The account is obtained in the first act; the larger story is what money becomes inside the Bushwick household—rent, food, sewing, laundry, small preferences, reciprocal debt, neighborhood exchange, and the ability to choose without settling every obligation immediately.
causalSpine: The provisional-status deadline forces the bank trip.
Identity and address create a bounded institutional obstacle that Carrie resolves in the first act.
Bjorn accepts Carrie's fifty only once it is named as debt rather than charity.
The account and debit card become meaningful only when the household must decide what limited money is for.
Astrid and the two male Kin begin to register as people with separate practical wants while still moving as a group at this stage.
The bodega and coffee-cart purchases convert abstract financial access into food, repair, laundry, pleasure, and reciprocal care.
Bjorn learns that a named, planned debt can remain unresolved without becoming dishonor.
The toaster remains a tangible comic payoff, but it becomes one useful household object rather than the proof that the bank story itself mattered.

issueCharacterState.Bjorn: Moves from treating debt as an immediate honor emergency toward carrying multiple obligations in order: household stability, food, and repayment. He distinguishes repayment from voluntary reciprocity when he buys Carrie coffee.
issueCharacterState.Carrie: Her bank competence resolves the institutional barrier quickly; the rest of the issue moves her into household budgeting and ordinary participation rather than repeated procedural combat.
issueCharacterState.Gunnar: Carries Issue 3 competence forward by building a household tally, but his contribution is memory and shared planning rather than mapping another institution.
issueCharacterState.Kin: Astrid and the two male Kin remain group-based in movement but begin expressing separate needs and preferences inside the household, preparing Issue 5's independent routines.
issueCharacterState.bankStaff: Ordinary employees working rationally inside a contemporary system; they occupy the first act rather than the whole issue.

continuity: The Bushwick apartment is already established home and proof-of-address friction arises because paperwork lags lived reality.
DTI documents are ordinary municipal paperwork.
The bank is an ordinary 2026 commercial environment.
Legacy S1E02 payload IDs remain stable production identifiers for this Issue 4 material.
readerOutcome: The reader should understand why the account matters, but more importantly see what it changes: the household can prioritize rent, choose groceries, repair clothing, wash clothes, buy one small pleasure, offer a neighbor something, and carry a debt over time. Financial participation becomes ordinary life rather than a 24-page banking puzzle.
